clue.text: Notorious publicity about Bali, perhaps

parts.note: PR, public relations, is publicity work
over can mean about, as in a quarrel over money

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of the island's name may be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A holiday island is getting a bad name in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bali' sits by 'perhaps' as if it were just an example of a place; 'perhaps' actually signals that its letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something proverbial is famous to the point of being a byword, which is what notorious means in its milder sense.

clue.text: Pious exercises for chanter

parts.note: pi is informal shorthand for pious, sanctimonious
PE, physical education, is school exercises

explanation.surface: Devout worshippers do religious exercises as they sing.
explanation.walkthrough: A chanter is the melody pipe of a set of bagpipes, so the definition hides behind the singing sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The chanter of a bagpipe is the fingered tube that plays the tune, a kind of musical tube.

clue.text: This once bought only little upfront

definitions.text: This once bought only little upfront

indicators.note: upfront asks for the leading letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A coin of old had very little buying power.
explanation.definitionFit: An obol was a small ancient Greek coin, so it once bought only a little.

clue.text: Print a view of Wapping?

parts.note: Wapping in east London was home to the Times and its sister papers; printing the paper's view there is writing a leader column

explanation.definitionFit: To editorialise is to express an opinion in print, as a newspaper's leading article does.

clue.text: Smelling of drink, bachelor sounds gloomy

indicators.note: sounds says the word for gloomy is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: eerie, weird and gloomy in atmosphere

explanation.surface: A single man reeks of booze and seems down.
explanation.definitionFit: Beery breath or a beery room carries the smell of ale.

clue.text: Sponge out oil left by coach

indicators.note: out says the letters are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone is cleaning oil left on a coach with a sponge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' shuffles OIL, L and COACH together.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge is slang for a heavy drinker, someone who soaks up liquor.

clue.text: Dirty at the front and at the back — like a brush?

indicators.note: at the front picks the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: aft is the nautical word for at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A brush is grubby at both ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'daft as a brush' means very silly, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The British simile daft as a brush makes silliness the brush's defining quality.

clue.text: The order going here from Il to 8?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'The order going here from Il to 8?'; 'Il to 8' is an OCR garble (perhaps Greek alpha to beta) that no source confirms
annotationWithheld.clue: The order going here from Il to 8?

clue.text: Stay afloat and take time to study the sea

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to read a subject is to study it at university
the water is a common way of saying the sea

explanation.surface: A swimmer rests in the sea, taking a moment to look around.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread water is to keep upright in deep water by moving the legs, staying afloat.

clue.text: State capital required to furnish new church

parts.note: to furnish is to provide or supply
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A capital city needs funds to equip a new church.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital is that of the US state of Rhode Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Providence is the capital city of the US state of Rhode Island.

clue.text: A little catnap, sensible in recess

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Taking a short nap in an alcove is a wise idea.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a vaulted recess at the end of a church, so the answer is one in a recess.

clue.text: Even a complete nonentity can't get lower than this

definitions.text: Even a complete nonentity can't get lower than this

parts.words: Even a complete nonentity can't get lower than this
parts.note: a total nobody is an utter zero, and the coldest possible temperature is the floor no thermometer can go below

explanation.definitionFit: Absolute zero is the lowest possible temperature, and figuratively a complete nothing.

clue.text: Assume posted information is correct, but get lost

definitions.meaning: read literally, trusting what is pinned up on a notice board
the idiom means to be abandoned or discarded

explanation.definitionFit: To go by the board is to be thrown overboard or abandoned; literally it is to rely on a notice board.

clue.text: Supporter of political theory derived from old oil digest

indicators.note: derived from says the answer is made by reworking the letters that follow

explanation.surface: A political thinker draws ideas from an old oil company digest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'derived from' rearranges O, OIL and DIGEST.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideologist is an adherent or theorist of a particular ideology.

clue.text: Like a graveyard that's too big one uses for redevelopment

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a size too big

indicators.note: redevelopment says the letters are rebuilt in another arrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cemetery that is too large is put to other uses.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is a clothing-size label; 'redevelopment' fits the graveyard picture while signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossiferous means containing bones, as the ground of a graveyard does.

clue.text: Notice given in girl's prayer book

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, here with its possessive s
a missal is the book of prayers for the Mass

explanation.surface: A note has been slipped into a young woman's prayer book.
explanation.definitionFit: A dismissal is notice given to an employee that their job is ending.

clue.text: Weight-lifter's tackle used by unqualified members

parts.note: sheer means utter or unqualified
legs are limbs, members of the body

explanation.surface: A strongman's gear is worked by sheer leg power.
explanation.walkthrough: Weight-lifter here is a lifting rig, not an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheerlegs are a hoist of two or three poles lashed at the top, used to lift heavy weights.

clue.text: Work cycle for Macbeth, perhaps

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
an era is an age or cycle of time

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare tragedy is part of a series of works.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's Macbeth is an example of an opera, signalled by perhaps.

clue.text: Gold that is left to an Oxford college

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A benefactor bequeaths gold to an Oxford college.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriel is one of the colleges of the University of Oxford.

clue.text: Scoop used in catering for a few customers

definitions.meaning: a news story that one paper alone has

explanation.definitionFit: Exclusive is both a newspaper scoop and select, catering only to a few.

clue.text: Puts too much importance on partner's hair? Not at first

indicators.note: Not at first drops the opening letter of the phrase

parts.note: a lover is a romantic partner
tresses are long locks of hair

explanation.surface: Someone fusses too much over a partner's hairstyle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not at first' removes the L from LOVERSTRESSES.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstress something is to lay too much emphasis or importance on it.

clue.text: Old county girl needed operation

parts.note: Sal is a short form of the girl's name Sally

explanation.surface: A young woman from the shires required surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: SALOP is the old name for Shropshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Salop was the former official name of the English county of Shropshire.

clue.text: Push off, using tiller mostly

indicators.note: mostly says the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a tiller is a shoot growing from the base of a plant

explanation.surface: Someone pushes a boat off with most of the tiller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tiller' looks like a boat's steering bar; it is the gardener's word for a shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoo is a command to go away, so push off as an imperative.

clue.text: Become strained from sudden attack without oxygen

indicators.note: without signals taking a letter away from the word

parts.note: a foray is a sudden raid or attack
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Nerves are frayed after an attack with no air supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerves or tempers fray when they become strained and worn.

clue.text: One answer left for a loved one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to do is to answer or serve, as in that will do

explanation.surface: Someone is left alone, answering for a sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is someone adored, a person greatly loved.

clue.text: Beautiful girl, if listened to, could be leader

indicators.note: listened to says the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful girl and whether means if

explanation.surface: A lovely young woman, if heard, might be in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A bellwether is the belled ram that leads a flock, hence any leader or trendsetter.

clue.text: Sort of force required for the job

definitions.meaning: a special military unit formed for one mission
a piece of work to be done

explanation.definitionFit: A task force is a kind of force, and a task is a job of work.

clue.text: Posh poly, for example, developing electoral studies

indicators.note: developing says the letters change into a new form

explanation.surface: Smart and less smart colleges develop courses in election studies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' rearranges POSH, POLY and EG. A poly was a British polytechnic college.
explanation.definitionFit: Psephology is the statistical study of elections and voting.
